lead: New Haven plumbing deals with old multi-family homes, cold winters and coastal flooding. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across New Haven.
risk: old galvanized and cast-iron pipes, frozen pipes and basement backups
risk_short: old pipes, frozen pipes and basement backups
why: East Rock, Wooster Square, the Annex and Fair Haven have two- and three-family homes from the 1880s to the 1930s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and old sewer laterals.
Winter cold freezes pipes near exterior walls and on porches. Coastal storms and heavy rain flood low areas near the harbor and back up basements.
utility: South Central Connecticut Regional Water Authority
water: New Haven's water comes from the Regional Water Authority, which uses reservoirs and wells. It is soft to moderately hard depending on the source.
tips: Know where each unit's shutoff is in a multi-family home.
Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
areas: PipeMend works in East Rock, Wooster Square, Westville, the Annex, Fair Haven, the Hill, Morris Cove and every other New Haven neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of New Haven Building Department, and plumbers are licensed by the Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection.

faq.a: The Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection licenses plumbers statewide. Permits for work in New Haven come from the city's Building Department.
